sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r6/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (read in memory via zipfile; sha256 6d44970b...; sheet 'Quality Checks' row 2 and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 2: #1 'instruction_is_a_natural_product_request' - 'The prompt reads like a real person asking for an app, not a spec sheet, checklist, or build recipe.'; no comments/threaded comments present, person list empty)
.qc-cache/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r6/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml lines 28-60 and criterion ids of all scored dimensions (to test lesson-12 one-to-one mirroring)
evidence: instruction.md read cold reads as a person asking for an app: opens 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' (L1), states the motivation ('Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled', L1), and describes needs in first person with reasons ('I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none', L3; 'If a message arrives while I am reading further up, leave my place alone', L7; 'Candidates sign in too... They must never see our internal notes', L9). No numbered acceptance list, shall/must table, feature matrix or endpoint list; normative words are sparse (must x2, never x3, should x2 across 665 words). L13 'Before you hand it over, please check it yourself the way we'll use it...' is the requester-voice check recommended by lesson 5. The build/runtime paragraph (L15-L19: Node/Express/SQLite, /app/server.js, port 3000, GET /api/health, /app/app.db, DB_PATH, accounts) is the template-mandated runtime contract (row 4 requires it stated) and is phrased as a request ('How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call'), not a build recipe replacing the product ask; it follows the product description rather than substituting for it. Layout and naming are explicitly left open (L11 'layout and names are yours'). Lesson 12 (notes read like an acceptance checklist mirroring criteria one-to-one) checked across every note: hireops_rules.md (2062 words) is written in the team's voice with reasons attached to rules, e.g. 'We like to know where a card was when it was rejected, because reopening takes it back to exactly that stage' (L50-51), 'Several of us work the same board, so every card carries a version' (L78), 'We're usually in the middle of something when an update lands, so it leaves alone the text I'm typing' (L127), 'Some conversations run long, so one opens on its most recent 30 messages' (L151), 'Candidates are outside the company, so nothing their browser receives may contain...' (L200), 'Our servers don't always start Node from inside the app folder... so please find your pages... relative to server.js' (L207-209); only 'never' x1 and 'always' x1 normative words. It does not mirror criteria one-to-one: e.g. hro_reject_reopen and hro_two_people (functional judge.toml L46-60) combine several notes sections, and the notes contain no step lists, suffixes, or probe values. integration.md L1-14 is byte-identical to the frozen template; the two task-added paragraphs (L16-23) give deployment reasons ('We copy /app as ordinary files when we deploy it, so...'). Weak/borderline elements considered and not judged defects: the HTTP status codes 401/403/404/409 in hireops_rules.md L22-24 and L80 and the card-version sentence L78 are API-contract flavoured, but each carries a user/business reason (e.g. 'so they can't even learn that it's there'; 'so whatever screen or tool sent the move can tell them'), are a small fraction of the notes, and sit in the notes rather than the prompt; the role table (L15-20) and candidate-wording table (L191-198) are domain data a real team would hand over. A cold reader would not mistake the prompt for a spec sheet. Counterexample attempts: (a) a reviewer flagging the runtime paragraph as a 'build recipe' would be contradicting the template-mandated contract and row 4; (b) the strongest Fail case is a portal reviewer reading hireops_rules.md section 3 'Two people at once' as an API spec because of '409' and 'version' wording - judged not to meet the defect bar since the reason is given and the behaviour is a genuine product need stated in the prompt (L3 'the refusal should say who'). Row 1 is a pure prose judgement; no runtime evidence is required for it, so none is missing.
